title: Spec-Driven Feature Development
competency: 02. Spec Framing - Requirements decomposition and testable specification creation
mission: Turn a vague and conflicting subscription request into an implementation-ready specification before any feature code is written.
domain: Subscription management with account roles, billing timing, prorated changes, pending requests, asynchronous provider results, and recovery states.
outcome: The learner proves that explicit clarification produces a safer, traceable specification than an agent's first unframed attempt.
seededDefects: The product request does not define what subscription management means.
Stakeholder notes conflict on permissions and when changes take effect.
Pending changes, asynchronous failures, retries, and recovery behavior are unresolved.
A coding agent can silently convert guesses into confident-looking requirements.
verificationGates: Three to five evidence-based clarifications cover authorization, billing, failure, and scope.
Requirements and acceptance criteria are testable and trace into the plan and tasks.
Before and after evidence uses the same agent conditions and contains genuine patches.
Starter application code and challenge evidence remain unchanged.
npm run verify:exercise checks protected inputs, implementation quality, and required submission evidence.
agentWorkflow: Capture an unframed specification attempt in a fresh agent session.
Inspect source code, stakeholder conflicts, and billing constraints.
Record confirmed decisions or explicit assumptions with consequences.
Generate the final specification in another fresh session under identical conditions.
Compare both results and stop before implementation.
Capture comparable before and after results using the conditions defined in the exercise README.
